positions.as_written: Expect this ligament to be torn after a true dislocation, and look for it rather than for a strain.
Assess lateral translation near extension, because that is the arc in which the ligament works.
Do not attribute instability in mid flexion to this ligament, because it is not tight there.
Avoid overtensioning, because a tight medial construct raises medial facet pressure and produces pain rather than stability.
Confirm the femoral attachment radiographically, since malposition changes the arc of restraint.
State that no measured optimum for graft tension exists, rather than quoting a figure as though it did.
Weigh the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations alongside the morphology.
